text: Stage 1: perceptual image compression §3.1, Appendix G The autoencoder follows VQGAN: an encoder ℰ maps an RGB image x ∈ ℝ H × W ×3 to z = ℰ( x ) ∈ ℝ h × w × c , a decoder 𝒟 reconstructs x̃ = 𝒟(ℰ( x )), and the downsampling factor is f = H / h = W / w = 2 m ( §3.1 ).
label: core

text: It is trained with a perceptual loss (LPIPS) plus a patch-based adversarial loss, which keeps reconstructions "confined to the image manifold by enforcing local realism and avoids bluriness introduced by relying solely on pixel-space losses such as L 2 or L 1 " ( §3.1 ).
label: core

text: L Autoencoder = min ℰ,𝒟 max ψ ( L rec ( x , 𝒟(ℰ( x ))) − L adv (𝒟(ℰ( x ))) + log D ψ ( x ) + L reg ( x ; ℰ, 𝒟) ) Equation 25 ( Appendix G ): D ψ is the patch discriminator, L reg one of the two regularisers below.
label: core

text: To avoid "arbitrarily high-variance latent spaces" the latent gets one of two mild regularisers ( §3.1 , Appendix G ): KL-reg. : a KL penalty towards a standard normal, as in a VAE, but weighted by about 10 −6 , so it is a barely regularised VAE (the released config sets kl_weight: 0.000001 , autoencoder config ).
label: core

text: VQ-reg. : a vector-quantisation layer with a large codebook, "absorbed by the decoder": the diffusion model works on z before quantisation, so the model "can be interpreted as a VQGAN" with the quantiser as the first layer of 𝒟.
label: core

text: Why it is cheap: every one of the tens to hundreds of denoising steps runs on f ² fewer spatial positions (16 times for f = 4, 64 for f = 8), while the latent stays a grid, so the UNet keeps its 2-D convolutional inductive bias ( §3.2 ).

text: Limitations and societal impact §5 The authors' own caveats: sampling is still sequential and "slower than that of GANs", and the autoencoder's reconstruction "can become a bottleneck for tasks that require fine-grained accuracy in pixel space"; they assume the super-resolution models are "already somewhat limited in this respect" ( §5 ).
label: core

text: On impact, cheaper training "democratize[s]" the technology and also makes it easier "to create and disseminate manipulated data or spread misinformation and spam", deep fakes disproportionately affect women, generative models can reveal their training data, and the two-stage approach may misrepresent the data in ways that remain "an important research question" ( §5 ).

text: DiT replaced the UNet with a Transformer on latent patches, using "an off-the-shelf pre-trained variational autoencoder (VAE) model from Stable Diffusion" ( DiT §5 ).
label: core

text: Stable Diffusion 3 moved to a rectified-flow objective and a Transformer but still denoises an f = 8 latent, now with 16 channels because "increasing the number of latent channels d significantly boosts reconstruction performance" ( SD3 §5.2.1 ); FLUX.1 is "a 12 billion parameter rectified flow transformer" on a 16-channel latent ( model card ).
label: core

text: Video and audio followed: Sora is "trained on and subsequently generates videos within this compressed latent space" ( Sora report ); Stable Video Diffusion ( arXiv 2311.15127 ), AudioLDM ( arXiv 2301.12503 ) and Stable Audio ( arXiv 2402.04825 ) are latent diffusion models by name.
label: depth

text: The old version of this page also counted Veo and many 3D and molecule systems; those are not checked against a source here (unconfirmed).
label: depth

text: The cross-attention interface became the standard plug for conditions: ControlNet adds spatial control by copying the encoder of a "locked" Stable Diffusion ( ControlNet ), and IP-Adapter adds image prompts through a "decoupled cross-attention mechanism" ( IP-Adapter ).
label: core

text: And the democratisation the paper aimed at happened: hobbyists fine-tune Stable Diffusion with low-rank adapters on its attention layers ( Hugging Face, LoRA for Stable Diffusion ).
